summary: This Dockerfile creates an Ubuntu container with the eza file listing tool pre-installed and configured. It sets up a demo directory with various file types, customizes the bash prompt to show a container indicator, and launches an interactive shell so you can see eza in action.

explanations.3: This tells the installer to run in non-interactive mode, so it won't pause asking for user input during setup.
explanations.5: The && chains commands together — if any step fails, the whole thing stops, which keeps the image clean and prevents partial installations.
explanations.6: The --no-install-recommends flag installs only essential packages, not optional extras, keeping the image smaller.
explanations.9: After installation, we delete the apt package cache to reduce the final image size since we won't need it again.
explanations.14: curl downloads the file, -fsSL means silent mode with error reporting, and the pipe | sends it directly to tar without saving it to disk first.
explanations.16: tar -xz extracts the compressed file (-z for gzip) and -C /usr/local/bin puts it where the system PATH can find it.
explanations.19: We're adding a bash alias that replaces the default ls command with eza, configured with several formatting flags.
explanations.24: mkdir -p creates parent directories if they don't exist, so /root/demo/src and /root/demo/docs can be created in one command.
explanations.28: dd copies 200 kilobytes of zeros to create a fake PDF file for demo purposes without wasting time.
explanations.35: The -i flag starts bash in interactive mode so you get a prompt instead of the container just exiting immediately.
